result.text: Title: Find a Job You have to regularly report, to which companies you wrote job applications.
Based on your job applications, new potential job offers are sent to you.
Companies have to confirm that they received job applications and rate the application.
A job interview can be negotiated.
When a company wants you to work for them, you enter the probation phase.
After probation phase, you can rate the company and the company can rate you.
Reviews for a company can only be seen (by job applicants) after 1 year.
If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless you rated the company C or less, then you continue to receive job offers, but no longer have to report.

In particular, connect an activity to the subsequent gateway, intermediate catch event, or end event rather than omitting the transition.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Only activities, gateways and events are sequence-flow endpoints. Never connect sequence flows to pools, lanes, data objects, groups or annotations.

result.rule: When the description presents activities in an order, states a decision outcome that leads to an activity, or identifies an event that determines what happens next.: Connect each stated transition with a sequence flow, including from the start event to the first activity, from each decision branch to its specified next step, and from an event-based gateway to its catching-event target.

When the description states that an activity is followed by a decision, synchronization, or cycle-exit condition, or that concurrent work begins after a preceding activity: Connect the activity to the relevant gateway with a sequence flow; for concurrent work, route the preceding flow through a parallel gateway that starts the concurrent branches.

When the description says that the process waits for a stated time or period to end before continuing: Model the wait as an intermediate catch timer event, then connect it to the subsequent activity rather than representing the passage of time as a task.

When the description says an activity occurs repeatedly or continues over an ongoing process and separately states that another activity starts only when a condition occurs: do not model the ongoing activity as an unconditional predecessor of the condition-triggered activity; preserve their distinct timing and stated dependencies in the BPMN flow

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description presents a decision whose possible outcomes are stated as conditions or answers: Label the corresponding gateway with a concise question that expresses the described decision, rather than a generic label that does not identify what is being decided.

When the description states a condition that distinguishes alternative branches: Label the gateway with the branch-controlling condition stated in the description, rather than with a separate downstream decision or activity.

When the description states that a process can end in one of multiple mutually exclusive outcomes: Model an exclusive gateway with a separate branch for each outcome, leading to the corresponding modeled outcome.

When the description presents multiple distinct activities as optional alternatives: Model each activity separately on an appropriate branch, rather than combining the alternatives into one activity, and preserve their connection to the subsequent flow.
